ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.claim: The primary addressees are Quraysh and, secondarily, the People of the Book: the latter claimed Moses and Abraham, while Quraysh treated Abraham as ancestor and religious leader.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r4.anchor: the addressees here are primarily the Quraysh and secondarily the People of the Book.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r7.claim: Abraham had no formal scripture; teachings were transmitted orally to both branches, preserved better among Israelites through prophets, blurred among illiterate Ishmaelites, and later included and partly altered in the Torah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r7.anchor: he did not have a scripture in the formal sense of the term. All his teachings were transmitted orally as traditions

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.claim: If “scriptures of Abraham” denotes texts preserving his teachings, the attribution remains correct even if later exegesis appears in them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p66/r1.anchor: if by the scriptures of Abraham (sws) the reference is to the ones in which his teachings are mentioned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p70/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p70/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p70/r1.claim: The passage adds extensions grounded in the original scriptural statement, a Qur’anic pattern that here turns the discourse from verse 40 onward into commentary on Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p70/r1.anchor: There are several examples in the Qur’ān in which a statement is cited and then certain additions are made in it

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r6.claim: Am lam yunabbaʾ means “rather, was he not informed?”; what follows is what is in the Torah, the scriptures of Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r6.anchor: أم لم ينبأ: أي بل ألم يخبر؟ بما في صحف موسى، وهي التوراة

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.claim: This section then turns to perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r17.anchor: transitions into a discussion of the perennial truths attested in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r1.claim: The scrolls passage and the statement that one burdened soul bears no other's burden correspond to 53:30–31, since both passages explain recompense.

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.claim: Rāzī proposes a shift from idolaters to scriptured people: a person with a book gave God's rights for a short time, then stopped when Muhammad came; the scrolls already taught individual accountability, so the man may be from the People of the Book.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r2.anchor: يمكن أن يقال : إن الله تعالى لما بين حال المشركين

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r1.claim: The verse tests the alternative excuse of complete ignorance: someone who fully knows needs no teaching, while one wholly unaware, like a sleeper, is not addressed; neither condition applies, so the turner is not excused.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r1.anchor: فقال : هذا المتولي هل علم الكل فجاز له التولي

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r2.claim: On one reading, the phrase means the teachings found in Moses' scrolls—such as monotheism and resurrection—so the Prophet's message of that content addresses both idolaters and People of the Book.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r2.anchor: أن يكون المراد ما فيها لا بصفة كونه فيها

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r3.claim: Alternatively, بما means the very contents as they stand in those scrolls, making the address specifically to the People of the Book who received those scriptures.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r3.anchor: أن المراد بما في الصحف مع كونه فيها

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r4.claim: The plural صحف most likely reflects numerous scrolls, not merely attribution to Moses and Abraham as dual possessors; the many tablets each count as a scroll.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r4.anchor: الظاهر أنها كثيرة ، قال الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.claim: The most apparent content is the rule that no bearer carries another's burden, though the phrase may cover more because the scrolls contain more than this alone.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r5.anchor: هو ما ذكر بقوله : { ألا تزر

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r6.claim: A second proposed content is that the afterlife is better than worldly life, as stated about the first scriptures in 87:18–19.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r6.anchor: هو أن الآخرة خير من الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r7.claim: A third view is that all foundational doctrines occur in every scripture; the command to follow earlier guidance concerns religious fundamentals, not legal branches that differ between communities.
RAZI-FULL:v29p12/r7.anchor: أصول الدين كلها مذكورة في الكتب بأسرها

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r1.claim: Rāzī first says eloquent speech needs no special rationale for naming Moses before Abraham; either order is valid.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r1.anchor: مثل هذا في كلام الفصحاء لا يطلب له فائدة

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r2.claim: As possible rationales, the earlier sūra orders the names by the scriptures' order of descent, whereas this passage addresses Jews first or names Moses first because his scrolls were numerous and familiar; Abraham's were less known.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r2.anchor: وأما ههنا فقد قلنا إن الكلام مع أهل الكتاب وهم اليهود

RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r3.claim: Rāzī says Moses is often mentioned later because the Prophet dealt largely with polytheists and Jews, while polytheists honored Abraham as their forefather.
RAZI-FULL:v29p13/r3.anchor: كثيرا ما ذكر الله موسى فأخر ذكره عليه السلام

STUDYQURAN:53:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r1.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r1.claim: Moses’ scriptures are named before Abraham’s despite chronology because they are more widely known.
STUDYQURAN:53:36/r1.anchor: the scrolls of Moses are here mentioned before those of Abraham (v. 37), because they are more widely known (Bḍ).

BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.claim: The alternative asks whether he is ignorant, never having been told what is in Moses' scrolls, meaning the books of the Torah.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.anchor: {أم} أهو جاهل {لم ينبأ} لم يخبر {بما فى صحف موسى} أي أسفار التوراة

BURSEVI:v9p201/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p201/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ṣaḥīfa as a flat spread surface, including the face or a writing sheet; its plurals are ṣaḥāʾif and ṣuḥuf, and a muṣḥaf gathers written sheets.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : الصحيفة المبسوطة من كل شيء كصحيفة الوجه والصحيفة التي كان يكتب فيها

BURSEVI:v9p201/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r5.speaker: القهستاتي
BURSEVI:v9p201/r5.claim: Al-Qahestātī says muṣḥaf can take any of three vowels on its mīm and denotes a collection containing the Quran.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r5.anchor: وقال القهستاتي : المصحف مثلث الميم ما جمع فيه قرآن

BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.speaker: أبو ذر الغفاري
BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.claim: Abū Dharr reports 104 revealed books: ten pages to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Idrīs, ten to Abraham, and the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Quran.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r12.anchor: وعن أبي ذر الغفاري رضي الله عنه قال : قلت : يا رسول الله كم من كتاب أنمل الله؟

BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.claim: Moses precedes Abraham by progression from the nearer and better-known figure; Moses truly had a revealed book, unlike Abraham.
BURSEVI:v9p201#2/r1.anchor: هو من باب الترقي من الأقرب إلى الأبعد لكون الأقرب أعرف وأيضا أن موسى صاحب كتاب حقيقة بخلاف إبراهيم

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r13.claim: The scrolls of Moses are the Torah.

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r14.claim: The scrolls of Abraham are the revelation sent down to him; their plural form indicates the many parts of that scripture.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r14.anchor: وصحف إبراهيم ما نزل عليه من الكتاب والجمع للإشارة إلى كثرته بكثرة أجزائه

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.claim: Abraham’s fulfillment means that he fully and perfectly discharged his duty of servitude.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r15.anchor: وتوفيته عليه السلام تأديته ما عليه من الحق في العبودية أتم التأدية وأبلغها

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.claim: The phrase about Abraham fulfilling his duty is illustrated by the verse saying he completed the trials imposed by his Lord.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r1.anchor: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن

TABATABAI:53:38-39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r2.claim: Although earlier Qur’an passages do not label these teachings as excerpts from the two scrolls, they present them as wisdom, admonitions, stories, and lessons; the question means whether he was told these scriptural teachings.
TABATABAI:53:38-39/r2.anchor: فمعنى الآيتين أم لم ينبأ بهذه الأمور وهي في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.claim: The reference is to the books of the Torah and the pages of Abraham; waffā means Abraham completed and fulfilled what he was commanded.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r13.anchor: أي بل ألم يخبر ولم يحدث بما في أسفار التوراة

THALABI:v9p151/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p151/r8.claim: The scrolls of Moses are the books of the Torah, and Abraham fulfilled his mission by conveying God’s message, including that no bearer bears another’s burden.
THALABI:v9p151/r8.anchor: يعني أسفار التوراة وإبراهيم الذي وفى ما أرسل به من تبليغ رسالة الله وهي قوله: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#2/r1.claim: The opening asks whether he has not been told or informed; the pages of Moses are the books of the Torah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65#2/r1.anchor: لم يحدث ولم يخبر {بما في صحف موسى} يعني: أسفار التوراة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r1.claim: The scriptures of Moses are the books of the Torah.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:36-44/r1.anchor: أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى } أسفار التوراة

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r4.claim: The scrolls of Moses refer to the Torah.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r4.anchor: Mûsâ’nın suhufundaki ile yani Tevrat ile

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan reports a view that before Abraham people were held liable for relatives' or masters' crimes; Abraham first rejected this, and from his law to Moses's law people were not charged with another's crime.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r6.anchor: Ebû Hayyân Bahr’da şöyle der: “Mûsâ ile İbrâhim, bu iki peygamberin tahsîsi için denilmiştir ki: Nûh ile İbrâhim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r1.claim: Following the criticism above, the passage recalls the core revelations given to Abraham and Moses, prophets about whom the audience knew most.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:36/r1.anchor: o sırada muhatapların hakkında en fazla bilgiye sahip oldukları peygamberlerden Hz. İbrâhim ve Hz. Mûsâ’ya indirilen vahiylerin özüne değinilmektedir

BURHAN:v3p239#4/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r6.claim: Moses precedes Abraham in 53:36 because the argument concerns abandonment and Moses's scriptures were more widely circulated; the order also accommodates the verse endings.
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r6.anchor: فإنما قدم ذكر موسى لوجهين أحدهما أنه في سياق الاحتجاج عليهم بالترك وكانت صحف موسى منتشرة أكثر انتشارا

NAHHAS:v4p276/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p276/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p276/r1.claim: The scriptural teaching includes that no person is punished in place of another.
NAHHAS:v4p276/r1.anchor: أنه لا يعذب أحد عن أحد

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.claim: Abraham fulfilled what he was commanded and tested with, including resolving to sacrifice his son, enduring his people's hostility and the fire, and circumcision.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r1.anchor: يقال إن إبراهيم - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وفى ما أمر به، وما امتحن به من ذبح ولده، فعزم على ذلك حتى فداه الله بالذبح

ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.claim: The question asks whether he was informed of what was in Moses' and Abraham's scrolls; the text then states the scrolls' contents.
ZAJJAJ:v5p75/r3.anchor: أي أم لم يخبر، ثم أعلم ما في الصحف

ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.claim: Asad cross-references 2:124 and says Moses and Abraham exemplify how prophets throughout history conveyed enduring ethical truths.
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n30/r1.anchor: Cf. 2:124 and the corresponding note 100. It is obvious that the names of Abraham and Moses are cited here only by way of example

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r1.claim: The definite “the right” refers to a particular justification for killing; the indefinite “any right” denies any justification, and is used to stress aggression.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r1.anchor: فإذا أراد تعالى أن يبين لنا العدوان يذكر (بغير حق)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r2.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r2.claim: Al-Kubaisi distinguishes al-nabiyyīn as a description of those being informed from al-anbiyāʾ as the plural of prophet after becoming one; the author adds “God knows best.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p763/r2.anchor: ويقول الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي عن معنى كلمة النبيين والأنبياء

QIRAAT-ER:53:36:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:53:36:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:53:36:3#1/r1.claim: Softening replaces the final hamza with long ā without changing meaning, and makes the word ending less abrupt.
QIRAAT-ER:53:36:3#1/r1.anchor: final hamza of yunabbaʾ replaced by long ā — phonetic variant without semantic change

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r1.claim: Am lam yunabba here means rather, has he not been informed?
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r1.anchor: ( أم لم ينبأ ( أي بل ألم يخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r2.claim: The scrolls of Moses are the Torah.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#4/r2.anchor: ( بما في صحف موسى ( وهي التوراة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r2.claim: The scrolls of Moses mean the books of the Torah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r2.anchor: لم يخبر {بما في صحف موسى} يعني: أسفار التوراة

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.claim: Moses is mentioned first because his tablets, the Torah, were more familiar and substantial to the audience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:36-38/r5.anchor: وتقديم موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام لأن صحفه وهي التوراة كانت أشهر وأكبر عندهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r7.claim: Moses’ scripture is named first because it was the greatest book after the Qurʾan and remained available for consultation; Abraham follows because Israelites and Arabs claimed his prophetic legacy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r7.anchor: ولما قدم كتاب موسى عليه السلام لكونه أعظم كتاب بعد القرآن مع أنه موجود بين الناس يمكن مراجعته , قال : { وإبراهيم }

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.speaker: دراج أبو السمح
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.claim: Darraj says the passage was revealed after a man who could not get a mount from the Prophet was offered transport by another man so he could catch the army.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.anchor: عن دراج أبي السمح قال: خرجت سرية غازية فسأل رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يحمله فقال: لا أجد ما أحملك عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r2.claim: The second interrogative shifts to another rebuke: if he rejects Muhammad, why not seek what earlier messengers taught about fearing God and escaping His punishment?
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r2.anchor: { أم } لإضراب الانتقال إلى متعجب منه وإنكار عليه آخر وهو جهله بما عليه أن يعلمه الذين يخشون الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r3.claim: The scrolls of Moses mean the Torah; Abraham's scrolls were written records of revelation, also named in the earlier-scriptures passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r3.anchor: و { صحف موسى } : هي التوراة ، وصحف { إبراهيم } : صحف سجل فيها ما أوحى الله إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r4.claim: Abu Dharr asked the Prophet about revealed books; the Prophet mentioned ten written scrolls given to Abraham.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r4.anchor: روى ابن حبان والحاكم عن أبي ذر أنه سأل النبي عن الكتب التي أنزلت على الأنبياء فذكر له منها عشرة صحائف أنزلت على إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r5.claim: Abraham is named because Arabs knew his religion as ḥanīfiyya, and some claimed to follow its traces, including Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r5.anchor: وإنما خص هذه الصحف بالذكر لأن العرب يعرفون إبراهيم وشريعته ويسمونها الحنيفية وربما ادعى بعضهم أنه على إثارة منها مثل : زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r6.claim: Moses's scrolls were familiar through the People of the Book among the Arabs, and the Qur'an records their demand that Muhammad receive what Moses received.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r6.anchor: وأما صحف موسى فهي مشتهرة عند أهل الكتاب ، والعرب يخالطون اليهود في خيبر وقريظة والنضير وتيما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r1.claim: Moses's scrolls precede Abraham's because they were renowned for their broader guidance and law; Abraham's surviving material was sparse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p130/r1.anchor: وتقديم { صحف موسى } لأنها اشتهرت بسعة ما فيها من الهدى والشريعة ، وأما صحف إبراهيم فكان المأثور منها أشياء قليلة .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r2.claim: Moses’s scrolls are the Torah; Abraham’s are books sent down from heaven.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r2.anchor: أي يعلم ما في صحف موسى وهي التوراة وفي صحف إبراهيم وهي كتب نزلت عليه من السماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#3/r1.claim: The scrolls of Moses here mean the Torah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى يعني التوراة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Thawri say Ibrahim fulfilled all that he was commanded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463#2/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير، والثوري أي بلغ جميع ما أمر به.

JISHUMI:v9p6661/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r1.claim: God holds each person accountable for his own sin, contrary to opponents; the cited scriptures are the books of Moses and Abraham.
JISHUMI:v9p6661/r1.anchor: ثم بين تعالى أنه يأخذ كل أحد بذنبه، خلاف ما قالوا، ردا عليهم على ما تقدم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427#2/r3.claim: صحف is also read with a light consonant.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r13.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r13.claim: A report through Abu Umama says Abraham fulfilled each day's worship with four midmorning rakas.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r13.anchor: وفى عمل كل يوم بأربع ركعات في أول النهار , رواه الهيثم عن أبي أمامة عن رسول الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r14.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r14.claim: A report through Anas and his father says Abraham recited the evening-and-morning glorification verse each morning and evening.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r14.anchor: أن يقول كلما أصبح وأمسى { فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون } الآية . رواه سهل بن معاذ عن أنس عن أبيه عن النبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r15.claim: Abraham fulfilled what his Lord commanded him in obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r15.anchor: وفيما أمر به من طاعة ربه , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r16.speaker: الهذيل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r16.claim: Al-Hudhayl says Abraham fulfilled this principle by opposing the earlier practice of holding a person liable for a child's or parent's offense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r16.anchor: كان بين نوح وإبراهيم يؤخذ الرجل بجريرة ابنه وأبيه فأول من خالفهم إبراهيم , قاله الهذيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r17.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r17.claim: Abraham performed every command given to him and fulfilled every vow.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r17.anchor: ما أمر بأمر إلا أداه ولا نذر إلا وفاه , وهذا معنى قول الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r18.claim: Abraham fulfilled the trials imposed on him: sacrificing his son, being cast into the fire, and being called a liar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r18.anchor: وفى ما امتحن به من ذبح ابنه وإلقائه في النار وتكذيبه

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r4.anchor: { بما في صحف موسى } [آية: 36] يعني التوراة كتاب موسى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#5/r1.claim: The scriptures of Moses mean the Torah; anbaʾa means to inform.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ أم لم ينبأ ﴾ بخبر ﴿ بما في صحف موسى ﴾ اى التوراة

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.claim: The reference is to Moses' and Abraham's scrolls, as also stated in al-Aʿla.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r1.anchor: أي صحف { وإبراهيم الذي وفى } كما في سورة «الأعلى»

QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.speaker: الهذيل ابن شرحبيل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.claim: These scrolls are singled out because, between Noah and Abraham, people were held liable for relatives' offenses.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:36-38/r2.anchor: وخص صحف إبراهيم وموسى بالذكر لأنه كان ما بين نوح وإبراهيم يؤخذ الرجل

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.claim: The unbeliever is asked whether he has heard what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, who fulfilled what was required of him in himself, wealth, and child.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r9.anchor: أم لم ينبأ هذا الكافر بما في صحف موسى ، وصحف إبارهيم الذي وفى ؛ أي أتم ما طولب به في نفسه وماله وولده

FARRA:v3p100/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p100/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p100/r5.claim: أم لم ينبأ means ألم ينبأ.
FARRA:v3p100/r5.anchor: ثم قال: «أم لم ينبأ» (36) المعنى: ألم.
